title: Uploading tax documents to an AI chatbot? Protect your data first
label: AI in tax

link.label: AI in accounting and tax 2026 guide (MFA)

lines: Leo uploaded his W-2 to a chatbot.
It showed his SSN and address.
Where does that file go now?

items.t: Black out SSNs and account numbers

items.s: Can it keep or train on your files?

beats.kicker: IRS tips to protect tax data

items.t: Encrypt and back up tax files

items.s: Helps block filing with your SSN.

cta.sub: We'll DM you our AI in accounting guide.

captions.instagram:
Thinking of uploading your W-2 or 1099 to an AI chatbot? Those forms carry your SSN, address and income.

✔️ Before you upload: black out SSNs and account numbers, and check the app's data settings.
✔️ IRS tips (IR-2026-119): turn on multifactor login, store tax records securely, encrypt and back up sensitive files, and consider an Identity Protection PIN.
✔️ The IRS's June 2026 AI guidance tells tax pros to handle client data only in secure, approved AI and never upload sensitive data to unsecured sites. A good rule for anyone.

Our AI in accounting guide covers safe ways to use AI with your finances.

sources.fact: IR-2026-119 (Oct. 2, 2026): turn on multifactor authentication, store digital tax records securely, encrypt sensitive files and back them up, consider an Identity Protection PIN; read 2026-10-30

IRS OPR Issue 2026-19 (June 24, 2026): 'Practitioners cannot rely solely on AI'; 'Practitioners must strictly handle all client data using only secure, enterprise-approved AI.' 'Never upload sensitive data to unsecured sites.'; read 2026-10-30
